name: Greta Hassan
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember discovering a half sister in the cut edge of a print.” Thursday often includes a stop at the entrance to the Wash House, where Greta stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: I am the half sister born later. Today's visit is the first time anyone explained the family photograph with a cut edge.
appearance: Greta is easy to recognize by short sandy hair and a marked widow's peak and fine brows over wide-set eyes. Usually dressed in a boxy denim jacket with one cuff folded back twice, Greta looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry when listening.
personality: Greta finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
agenda: To meet the half sister outside the old photograph.
family: Mika Drew is Greta’s second cousin. Greta chooses whether to use it. Mika saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *Window seven*, Mika says, “The rail squealed when I moved it and woke three people.”
connections: Owen Kerr. Buying familiar food introduces the younger sister to a childhood she did not share. Also in the story is Iva Salas (older half sister).
